why: E19 (PRED-018) found that fragmentation acts on the policy ranking mostly as a load increase (P5 PASS), with one residual: trace_like rho 0.6 pi 0.2 first_fit, R_fcfs 1.66 against R_srpt 1.15 (gap 0.50). E19's control had two weaknesses found after grading: (1) it scaled every arrival instead of the jobs fragmentation actually slowed; (2) deg_load = J(rho_eff)/J(rho) at unit durations omits the slower service itself, so R mixed the service-time inflation into the residual. E20 replaces it with pi = 0 arms that carry exactly F's GPU-work and asks where the fcfs residual comes from.

already_known: FCFS waiting time grows with service-time variability (Pollaczek-Khinchine for M/G/1; Kingman's approximation for G/G/c); SRPT is far less sensitive (Schrage 1968; Harchol-Balter 2013). So P4 (within-class spread hurts fcfs) is expected from known theory.

Multiserver-job FCFS has head-of-line blocking and its stability region depends on the job mix (Brill and Green 1984; Grosof, Harchol-Balter, Scheller-Wolf, e.g. 'Stability for two-class multiserver-job systems' and 'WCFS', 2022-2023). Inflating wide jobs lengthens blocking.

Queues whose service rate depends on the system state (load-dependent service, e.g. contention slowdowns) are a classical topic; state-dependent degradation creating positive feedback near saturation is known in general terms. Not checked for the specific fragmentation-placement coupling.
Fragmentation hurts and consolidated placement helps (Tiresias NSDI 2019, Philly ATC 2019, Gandiva OSDI 2018).
prior_art.what_is_not_claimed_new: That FCFS is variance-sensitive; that wide-job inflation hurts MSJ FCFS; that fragmentation hurts.
prior_art.candidate_contribution: Within the MSJ model with node locality: a decomposition of fragmentation's extra fcfs delay into state coupling, within-class spread and between-class composition, at exactly matched GPU-work. Novelty UNKNOWN.
prior_art.search_done: Recall only; no systematic search before sealing.

seen: All of E19 (seeds 1901-1903), including per-seed fcfs J at trace_like rho 0.6 pi 0.2 (3.685, 2.922, 2.689; alpha 0.086-0.141) and the load arm. The residual this seal tests was found there; E20 uses new seeds 2001-2006.

Before writing the predictions, from E19 numbers: util_over_rho at pi 0.2 is about 1.33 for both policies, so a rough expectation of Q_fcfs ~ 3.1 / (1.33 x 1.88) ~ 1.24 and Q_srpt ~ 1.25 / (1.33 x 1.09) ~ 0.86 (gap ~0.38). This back-of-envelope used E19's J(0.8) at unit durations and is not E20 data.

seal_integrity.not_seen: No E20 metric on seeds 2001-2006; no JCT of any CS, CM or U arm on any seed; no rho 0.55 run in any experiment at pi > 0.
seal_integrity.timestamp: Local git commit only; no external timestamp.

measurand_validity.model: As E19: N=64, 8-GPU nodes, trace_like mix (needs 1/2/4/8/16/32, probs .50/.20/.15/.10/.04/.01), exponential sizes mean 1, sigma 0, penalty_mode excess, rate = 1/(1 + pi * excess_nodes), sticky first_fit placement, no migration, placement never blocks admission.
measurand_validity.arms: F = fragmented run at pi. All other arms are pi = 0 runs on the same arrivals, needs and sizes with job durations multiplied: RP by each job's realised slowdown 1/rate_j in F; CS by those slowdowns permuted within need class (rng seed + 7,000,000); CM by the class's GPU-work-weighted mean slowdown; U by the overall GPU-work-weighted mean slowdown. RP, CM and U carry exactly F's GPU-work; CS within 0.5% (pilot). The scheduler sees the arm's durations as sizes (sigma 0).
measurand_validity.why_RP_is_forced_for_fcfs: fcfs is non-preemptive and admits by free-GPU count only; placement never blocks admission. Given realised durations the schedule is identical, so RP = F is an instrument check, not a finding.
measurand_validity.srpt: srpt is preemptive and re-places jobs; its F slowdown uses the job's final rate, so srpt's U carries F's work only approximately. srpt gets only BASE, F and U.
measurand_validity.statistics: Q = J_F / J_U per seed (residual against exact uniform work, including the slower service). For fcfs: a = log(J_F/J_CS) state coupling (slowdowns tied to the cluster state at placement), b = log(J_CS/J_CM) within-class spread, c = log(J_CM/J_U) between-class composition; T = log(J_F/J_U) = a + b + c. Seed-paired, 80k horizon, shares on seed means.

experiment.analysis: analyze_e20.py (written and sealed with this file)
experiment.grid: trace_like, first_fit, rows (rho, pi) in {(0.55, 0.2), (0.6, 0.2), (0.6, 0.1)} x seeds 2001-2006 x horizons {40k, 80k}; fcfs arms BASE, F, RP, CS, CM, U; srpt arms BASE, F, U. 72 tasks, 648 simulations.

detector.label: DIVERGING if aborted/time limit or alpha >= 0.8; STABLE if alpha <= 0.2; else UNKNOWN. A cell (policy, rho, pi, arm) is labelled only when all six seeds agree.
detector.status: alpha is unaudited near a boundary (U-31). E19's fcfs F at rho 0.6 pi 0.2 had alpha 0.086-0.141, so that cell may come out UNKNOWN on six seeds; rho 0.55 pi 0.2 is in the decision rows for that reason. UNKNOWN cells make the statistic unscorable; they are not relabelled.

predictions.P0: Instrument (forced): fcfs RP mean JCT equals F within relative 1e-9 in every run. Failure stops the episode as R3.
predictions.P1: The residual replicates against the exact-work control: at (0.6, 0.2), seed-mean Q_fcfs - Q_srpt >= 0.2 and every one of the six seeds > 0. Unscorable if any of fcfs F/U, srpt F/U is not STABLE.
predictions.P2: DECISION. State coupling carries at least half of the fcfs residual: in every decision row ((0.55, 0.2), (0.6, 0.2)) where fcfs F, CS, CM, U are STABLE and mean T > 0, mean a >= 0.5 * mean T. At least one such row.
predictions.P3: Composition hurts fcfs: mean c > 0 in every scorable decision row.
predictions.P4: Within-class spread hurts fcfs (expected from known theory): mean b >= 0 in every scorable decision row. Low resolution expected; report b in SE units.
predictions.P5: The residual grows with pi: at rho 0.6, mean T(pi 0.2) > mean T(pi 0.1).

pre_committed_consequence.P1_fail_or_T_le_0: E19's fcfs residual does not survive an exact-work control on new seeds. Record it as an artefact of the approximate control or of seed noise; close the residual thread; H10 stays a level effect with no fragmentation-specific term.
pre_committed_consequence.P2_pass: Most of fcfs's extra delay under fragmentation comes from the coupling between fragmentation and the cluster state (slowdowns land when the cluster is busy), which no static work-distribution model reproduces. Record as a candidate fragmentation-specific mechanism within this model, with srpt's insensitivity beside it. Next would be measuring the coupling directly (slowdown vs occupancy at placement).
pre_committed_consequence.P2_fail_c_largest: The residual is mostly composition: fragmentation inflates wide jobs and MSJ FCFS is sensitive to wide-job size. This is a change of job-size distribution, i.e. known theory; record no fragmentation-specific dynamic.
pre_committed_consequence.P2_fail_other: Report the three shares as measured and do not name a mechanism.
pre_committed_consequence.P2_unscorable: If no decision row is scorable, say that the decomposition was not answered; do not interpret Q.

declared_unknowns: Whether CS removes all state coupling: permuting within class also breaks any correlation of slowdown with the job's arrival order inside a busy period, which is part of what a counts.
srpt's U arm work match (final rate only).
